topic: Euler’s Identity: The Most Beautiful Equation
target_audience: High school students or math enthusiasts with basic trigonometry and complex number knowledge.

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Complex Plane
lecture_lines: The complex plane has real and imaginary axes.
A point (a, b) maps to a + bi.
We can represent this point using distance and angle.
animations: Display modulus r (#FFFF00) and angle theta (#00FFFF).

sections.title: The Power of Rotation
lecture_lines: Multiplying by i rotates ninety degrees counter-clockwise.
Exponential functions act as growth operators.
e to the ix is a rotation operator.
animations: Display unit circle #FFFFFF in complex plane.

sections.title: Deriving Euler’s Formula
lecture_lines: Euler's Formula relates exponentials to trig functions.
e to the ix equals cos x plus i sin x.
This formula describes motion along the unit circle.
As x grows, the point traverses the circumference.
This connects the exponential and trigonometric worlds.
animations: Show Taylor series for e^x, cos x, sin x.
Substitute x = i*theta into Taylor series.
Group real terms as cos theta (#00FF00).
Group imaginary terms as i sin theta (#00FFFF).

sections.title: The Grand Finale: e^(πi) = -1
lecture_lines: Plug pi into the formula for x.
cos pi is negative one; sin pi is zero.
The equation becomes e to the pi i equals -1.
This represents a half-turn around the origin.
We have reached our destination: e to the pi i plus 1 equals 0.

sections.title: Summary and Elegance
lecture_lines: This equation connects five fundamental constants.
It unites arithmetic, geometry, and analysis.
Truly the most beautiful equation in mathematics.
